brief: Design an interface for a "temporal email client" where messages exist as physical objects falling through a vertical space at different speeds based on their urgency and emotional weight—urgent email

dominant_strengths: Conceptual metaphor of falling shapes as weighted messages is genuinely novel and invites kinetic engagement
Restrained dark palette with limited accent colors keeps focus on the falling-object choreography
dominant_weaknesses: Reads as an arcade catch-game, not an email client—no sender, subject, or message affordance is legible
Typography is generic uppercase tracked labels in corners; lacks hierarchy, weight variation, or informational density
Spatial composition feels sparse and arbitrary; shapes float without rhythm, scale logic, or urgency mapping cues
fix_priorities: Attach actual message metadata (sender, snippet, time-to-decay) to each falling object so the metaphor carries content
Establish a visual language mapping color/shape/speed to urgency and emotional weight with a legend or onboarding
Refine typography system with a numeric weight readout, status row, and consistent type scale beyond corner labels
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral concept is intriguing but behavioral utility collapses—you cannot actually read or act on email—leaving only thin reflective novelty.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits: the falling-object metaphor exists, but without message content or interaction model it functions as a toy rather than an email client.
